pillar_reactions.evidence: After the training and mobility block the prospect tied it directly to his own stated goal: 'I like that. Yep. That's exactly how, yep. I mean, cause that's exactly where I'm trying to get to be completely honest.' He had already volunteered the frame himself earlier — 'I want to be able to perfect it before I start doing something and go and guess on what I'm doing.'
Agreed without questions or pushback: 'Exactly. Makes sense. Yeah, 100%.' He had already described his own diet as clean and had no follow-up on the eating-window mechanic.

Understood and agreed, no clarifying questions: 'Right.' then 'Quite a bit of information, but I hope that it all makes sense... Yeah, 100%. Love it.' He did not probe the video-review loop, the app or the Thursday live workout.

anchors.raw: I'm not paying 85, you know, $70 to $100 a freaking month to go to the gym and just hope and pray that I get to where I want to be
anchors.note: His entire reference frame for spending on fitness is $70-100 per month, and he framed even that as bad value. $6,000 for six months is roughly 10x his mental ceiling, and the rep never repositioned against this anchor.

anchors.raw: I've got a 26-pounder, I've got a 35-pounder, a 44-pounder, and a 53-pounder
anchors.note: He had already bought four kettlebells before the call — evidence of committed spend and intent. The rep noted it but never used it as a buying-behaviour signal.

anchors.raw: my total per month would probably, I mean, I'd probably say, man, probably like a, I don't even know, better safe than sorry, probably like 150, 200 bucks, just easy spend
anchors.note: Self-reported discretionary capacity of $150-200 per month against a $1,000/month equivalent. This was discoverable in Phase 2 and was only surfaced 48 minutes into the call.

unmet_demand.want: One-to-one kettlebell coaching at a price payable from roughly $150-200 per month, with no lump sum and no financing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is $6,000 upfront or a third-party financed equivalent; the only in-budget product is the $200/month group community, which removes the one-to-one form correction that was his stated reason for the call.

unmet_demand.want: A specific fix for wrist pain during overhead kettlebell pressing, possibly caused by an undiagnosed arthritic condition
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme has no clinical assessment pathway; the rep answered it as a form issue without anyone examining the wrist.
